source.title: Diva Hero vs Vayu Turbo | IMN Finals Tournament Match | Yugioh Edison Format
source.match: Vayu Turbo won game 1; Diva Hero won games 2 and 3

notes: Commentary and viewer views are paraphrased human opinion, not ground truth.
Each position is read from video frames and auto-captions, then checked against the board and duel log.
actor_knows is the only part an engine may see. replay_only is what the replay view adds and must never be given to a policy.
Timestamps are approximate, within about 15 seconds.
Hand lists are read from a cropped view. hand_complete says whether every card in the hand was confirmed.

positions.decision: Choose which monster Trap Dustshoot shuffles from the revealed hand
positions.played_evidence: Stratos is absent from the next visible hand; the other five cards remain.

commentary.summary: Calls all three good options and weighs how each runs into the set Torrential Tribute and Ryko.

positions.decision: Choose the card to banish with Gold Sarcophagus
positions.options_note: Any card left in the deck. The full decklist is not captured here.

commentary.summary: Raises Future Fusion to send Destiny HERO - Malicious, then discusses why the player chose Reinforcement of the Army instead. Part of this reasoning was lost between captions.

positions.decision: Main Phase play with a suspected Ryko on the opposing field
positions.options_note: Includes setting Torrential Tribute, activating Heavy Storm, summoning Deep Sea Diva, or combinations.
positions.played: Set Torrential Tribute and pass without summoning

commentary.summary: Reads the set monster as probably Ryko and questions exposing Torrential Tribute to it.

positions.what_happened: On the next turn Torrential Tribute is in the actor's Graveyard and the opponent's Graveyard has grown, consistent with Ryko destroying it and milling.

positions.decision: Activate Heavy Storm into four set cards before summoning

commentary.summary: Points out the Heavy Storm runs into Solemn Judgment; gives no clear verdict on the play.

positions.what_happened: Solemn Judgment negates it, taking the opponent to 4000. Stratos then searches Destiny HERO - Malicious.

positions.decision: Choose which monster Trap Dustshoot shuffles from the revealed hand

commentary.summary: Treats taking Dark Grepher as a strong pick.

viewer_comment.summary: One viewer argues Malicious was better because it leaves Grepher, Miracle Fusion and Mind Control much weaker.

positions.decision: Follow-up after Pulling the Rug stops Deep Sea Diva's effect, with Mind Control available
positions.options_note: Mind Control could target either opposing monster. Mind Control's monster cannot attack.
positions.played: Mind Control on Dark Grepher, discard Malicious to send Plaguespreader Zombie, then Miracle Fusion for Elemental HERO Absolute Zero

commentary.summary: Follows the line as a natural answer to losing Grepher, and notes Zero can attack while the controlled monster cannot.

positions.what_happened: Absolute Zero (2500) attacks and destroys Blackwing Armed Wing.

positions.decision: Respond to the Summon of Elemental HERO Stratos with a set Bottomless Trap Hole, or hold it

commentary.summary: Remarks that Bottomless is not used on Stratos and that its value has changed; the caption ends before the full reasoning.

positions.what_happened: Stratos searches Elemental HERO Neos Alius and attacks for 1800.
positions.identification_note: The set card is identified from face-down artwork in this replay view and the caption; confirm before relying on it.

positions.decision: Main Phase 2 play after attacking, holding Dark Grepher and Elemental HERO Neos Alius
positions.options_note: Includes setting Dark Grepher, summoning Neos Alius, or adding no monster.
positions.played: Set Dark Grepher, keeping Neos Alius

commentary.summary: First says the reason is unclear, then suggests it can draw out Torrential Tribute and leave Neos Alius as a follow-up.

rejected.topic: Stardust Dragon and Absolute Zero attack sequence
rejected.reason: Could not determine which card Stardust Dragon responded to. Dimensional Prison banishes rather than destroys, so it should not qualify for Stardust's effect, yet the commentary centers on it. Recording this would mean guessing.
